### Defined types

## Classes

### <a name="borgmatic"></a>`borgmatic`

The configurations themselves are borgmatic::config resources and their
schedules borgmatic::timer resources, declared directly or through the
`configs` and `timers` hashes.

#### Examples

##### A configuration backed up every night

```puppet
include borgmatic

borgmatic::config { 'system':
  source_directories    => ['/etc', '/home', '/root', '/var'],
  repositories          => ['ssh://borg-client1@backup.example.org/srv/borg/client1'],
  encryption_passphrase => Sensitive('correct horse battery staple'),
  keep_daily            => 7,
}

borgmatic::timer { 'system':
  on_calendar => '*-*-* 01:00:00',
}
```

### <a name="borgmatic--server"></a>`borgmatic::server`

Installs Borg and manages the directory holding the repositories. The
repositories and the SSH keys allowed to reach them are
borgmatic::repository and borgmatic::authorized_key resources, declared
directly, through the `repositories` and `authorized_keys` hashes or
collected from the resources exported by the clients.

#### Examples

##### A server collecting the repositories exported by its clients

```puppet
class { 'borgmatic::server':
  base_path => '/srv/borg',
  group     => 'borgmatic',
  mode      => '0750',
}

Borgmatic::Repository <<| tag == "borgmatic_${facts['networking']['fqdn']}" |>>
Borgmatic::Authorized_key <<| tag == "borgmatic_${facts['networking']['fqdn']}" |>>
```

## Defined types

### <a name="borgmatic--authorized_key"></a>`borgmatic::authorized_key`

Adds to the authorized_keys file of `user` a line forcing `borg serve`
with the given restrictions. The line is matched on the key type and
body, so a key can only be authorized once per file.

Without `restrict_to_paths` nor `restrict_to_repositories`, the key
reaches every repository `user` can read.

#### Examples

##### An append-only key for a monitoring user

```puppet
borgmatic::authorized_key { 'client1_monitoring':
  user              => 'borg-client1-check',
  key               => 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExample nrpe@client1',
  restrict_to_paths => ['/srv/borg/client1'],
  append_only       => true,
}
```

#### Parameters

* [`key`](#-borgmatic--authorized_key--key)

* [`restrict_to_paths`](#-borgmatic--authorized_key--restrict_to_paths)
* [`restrict_to_repositories`](#-borgmatic--authorized_key--restrict_to_repositories)
* [`append_only`](#-borgmatic--authorized_key--append_only)

Public key, `<type> <base64> [comment]`.

Whether the key is present or absent.

##### <a name="-borgmatic--authorized_key--target"></a>`target`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

authorized_keys file, `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` for root and
`/home/<user>/.ssh/authorized_keys` otherwise by default. Its directory
must exist.

##### <a name="-borgmatic--authorized_key--restrict_to_paths"></a>`restrict_to_paths`

Data type: `Array[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

`--restrict-to-path` values: the repositories the key reaches must be

##### <a name="-borgmatic--authorized_key--restrict_to_repositories"></a>`restrict_to_repositories`

Data type: `Array[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

`--restrict-to-repository` values: the repositories the key reaches.

Default value: `[]`

Data type: `Boolean`

Pass `--append-only`: the key can add archives but not delete them.

Default value: `false`

Umask of `borg serve`, which sets the mode of the files it writes.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--authorized_key--storage_quota"></a>`storage_quota`

### <a name="borgmatic--config"></a>`borgmatic::config`

Writes `<config_dir>/<title>.yaml` in the flat format read by borgmatic
1.8 and later. Every borgmatic option set to a value other than undef is
rendered under its borgmatic name, in the order of the borgmatic
reference. Options without a parameter of their own go in `options`.

An option is only understood by the borgmatic releases that know it:
`commands`, for instance, needs borgmatic 2.0, whose older
`before_*`/`after_*` hooks are deprecated but still supported. With
`validate`, the file is checked by the installed borgmatic before being
replaced.

* **See also**
  * https://torsion.org/borgmatic/reference/configuration/

#### Examples

##### Back up a host to two servers

```puppet
borgmatic::config { 'system':
  source_directories    => ['/etc', '/home', '/root', '/var'],
  exclude_patterns      => ['/var/cache', '/var/tmp'],
  repositories          => [
    { 'path' => 'ssh://borg-client1@backup1.example.org/srv/borg/client1', 'label' => 'backup1' },
    { 'path' => 'ssh://borg-client1@backup2.example.org/srv/borg/client1', 'label' => 'backup2' },
  ],
  encryption_passphrase => Sensitive('correct horse battery staple'),
  keep_daily            => 7,
  keep_weekly           => 4,
  keep_monthly          => 6,
  checks                => [{ 'name' => 'repository', 'frequency' => '2 weeks' }],
  healthchecks          => 'https://hc-ping.com/your-uuid-here',
}
```

##### Dump the MariaDB databases

```puppet
borgmatic::config { 'databases':
  repositories      => ['ssh://borg-client1@backup1.example.org/srv/borg/client1-db'],
  mariadb_databases => [{ 'name' => 'all', 'username' => 'backup', 'password' => Sensitive('secret') }],
}
```

### <a name="borgmatic--repository"></a>`borgmatic::repository`

The repository directory is created with the given owner, group and
mode, then initialised by `borg init` (Borg 1.x) running as root, the
files it wrote being handed over to the owner. An existing repository is
left alone: changing `encryption` or `passphrase` afterwards has no
effect on it, and removing the resource keeps it on disk.

Clients usually export this resource, tagged for their backup server,
which collects it after declaring borgmatic::server.

#### Examples

##### A repository reachable by the root key of a client

```puppet
borgmatic::repository { 'client1':
  owner           => 'borg-client1',
  passphrase      => Sensitive('correct horse battery staple'),
  authorized_keys => {
    'root' => {
      'key' => 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExample root@client1',
    },
  },
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `borgmatic::repository` defined type:

* [`path`](#-borgmatic--repository--path)
* [`owner`](#-borgmatic--repository--owner)
* [`group`](#-borgmatic--repository--group)
* [`mode`](#-borgmatic--repository--mode)
* [`encryption`](#-borgmatic--repository--encryption)
* [`passphrase`](#-borgmatic--repository--passphrase)
* [`umask`](#-borgmatic--repository--umask)
* [`append_only`](#-borgmatic--repository--append_only)
* [`storage_quota`](#-borgmatic--repository--storage_quota)
* [`authorized_keys`](#-borgmatic--repository--authorized_keys)

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--path"></a>`path`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Path of the repository, `<base_path>/<title>` by default where
`base_path` comes from borgmatic::server.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--owner"></a>`owner`

Data type: `String[1]`

User owning the repository, the one borgmatic logs in as.

Default value: `'root'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--group"></a>`group`

Data type: `String[1]`

Group of the repository, the owner by default.

Default value: `$owner`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--mode"></a>`mode`

Data type: `Stdlib::Filemode`

Mode of the repository directory.

Default value: `'0700'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--encryption"></a>`encryption`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Encryption]`

Encryption mode passed to `borg init`, the `encryption` of
borgmatic::server by default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--passphrase"></a>`passphrase`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Secret]`

Passphrase of the repository key, required unless `encryption` is
`none`. It must match the `encryption_passphrase` of the client.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--umask"></a>`umask`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Umask]`

Umask of `borg init`, for example `0027` to let the group read the
repository. It is also the default umask of `authorized_keys`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--append_only"></a>`append_only`

Data type: `Boolean`

Create the repository in append-only mode.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--storage_quota"></a>`storage_quota`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::StorageQuota]`

Storage quota of the repository, for example `500G`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--repository--authorized_keys"></a>`authorized_keys`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Hash[String[1], Any]]`

borgmatic::authorized_key resources reaching this repository, keyed by
a name unique within it. Their `user` defaults to `owner`,
`restrict_to_paths` to `path` and `umask` to `umask`.

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="borgmatic--timer"></a>`borgmatic::timer`

Declares the `borgmatic-<title>.service` oneshot unit running borgmatic
for one configuration file or directory, and the
`borgmatic-<title>.timer` unit starting it. With `persistent`, a run
missed while the host was off happens at the next boot, which a cron job
cannot do. The service runs with a low CPU and I/O priority.

Logging flags are command line options rather than configuration
options because borgmatic only reads them from the configuration since
version 2.0.

#### Examples

##### Nightly backups logged to a file

```puppet
borgmatic::timer { 'system':
  on_calendar        => '*-*-* 01:00:00',
  verbosity          => -1,
  syslog_verbosity   => 1,
  log_file           => '/var/log/borgmatic/system.log',
  log_file_verbosity => 1,
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `borgmatic::timer` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-borgmatic--timer--ensure)
* [`config`](#-borgmatic--timer--config)
* [`on_calendar`](#-borgmatic--timer--on_calendar)
* [`enable`](#-borgmatic--timer--enable)
* [`persistent`](#-borgmatic--timer--persistent)

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

Whether the units are present or absent.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--config"></a>`config`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Configuration file or directory to run, `<config_dir>/<title>.yaml` by
default where `config_dir` comes from class borgmatic.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--on_calendar"></a>`on_calendar`

Data type: `Variant[String[1], Array[String[1], 1]]`

When to run, as one or more systemd `OnCalendar` expressions.

Default value: `'daily'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--enable"></a>`enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to enable and start the timer. When false the units are kept,
so the service can still be started by hand or by another unit.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--persistent"></a>`persistent`

Data type: `Boolean`

Run at boot when a run was missed while the host was off.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--randomized_delay_sec"></a>`randomized_delay_sec`

Data type: `Optional[Systemd::Timespan]`

Random delay added to each run, to spread the load of several timers.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--actions"></a>`actions`

Data type: `Array[Borgmatic::Action]`

Actions to run, borgmatic runs its default actions (create, prune,
compact and check) when empty.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--verbosity"></a>`verbosity`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Verbosity]`

`--verbosity` flag, the console output ending up in the journal.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--syslog_verbosity"></a>`syslog_verbosity`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Verbosity]`

`--syslog-verbosity` flag.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--log_file"></a>`log_file`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

`--log-file` flag.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--log_file_verbosity"></a>`log_file_verbosity`

Data type: `Optional[Borgmatic::Verbosity]`

`--log-file-verbosity` flag.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--extra_args"></a>`extra_args`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Other borgmatic flags, placed before the actions.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--nice"></a>`nice`

Data type: `Integer[-20, 19]`

`Nice` of the service.

Default value: `19`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--cpu_scheduling_policy"></a>`cpu_scheduling_policy`

Data type: `Enum['other', 'batch', 'idle', 'fifo', 'rr']`

`CPUSchedulingPolicy` of the service.

Default value: `'batch'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--io_scheduling_class"></a>`io_scheduling_class`

Data type: `Enum['realtime', 'best-effort', 'idle']`

`IOSchedulingClass` of the service.

Default value: `'best-effort'`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--io_scheduling_priority"></a>`io_scheduling_priority`

Data type: `Integer[0, 7]`

`IOSchedulingPriority` of the service.

Default value: `7`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--unit_entry"></a>`unit_entry`

Data type: `Systemd::Unit::Unit`

Settings merged into the `[Unit]` section of the service.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--service_entry"></a>`service_entry`

Data type: `Systemd::Unit::Service`

Settings merged into the `[Service]` section of the service. An empty
string resets a setting to the systemd default, for example
`{ 'Nice' => '' }`.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-borgmatic--timer--timer_entry"></a>`timer_entry`

Data type: `Systemd::Unit::Timer`

Settings merged into the `[Timer]` section of the timer.

Default value: `{}`

## Functions

### <a name="borgmatic--contains_sensitive"></a>`borgmatic::contains_sensitive`

Type: Puppet Language

Tells whether data holds a Sensitive value, at any depth

#### `borgmatic::contains_sensitive(Any $data)`

The borgmatic::contains_sensitive function.

Returns: `Boolean` Whether a Sensitive value was found.

##### `data`

Data type: `Any`

The data to inspect.

### <a name="borgmatic--normalize"></a>`borgmatic::normalize`

Type: Puppet Language

Drops the undef values of hashes and arrays and unwraps the Sensitive
values, recursively. Key order is preserved.

#### `borgmatic::normalize(Any $data)`

Drops the undef values of hashes and arrays and unwraps the Sensitive
values, recursively. Key order is preserved.

Returns: `Any` The data without undef nor Sensitive values.

##### `data`

Data type: `Any`

The data to normalise.

### <a name="borgmatic--to_yaml"></a>`borgmatic::to_yaml`

Type: Puppet Language

Undef options are left out and long values are never folded. The result
is Sensitive when the configuration holds a Sensitive value, such as the
encryption passphrase, so that it stays out of logs and reports.

#### `borgmatic::to_yaml(Hash[String[1], Any] $config)`

Undef options are left out and long values are never folded. The result
is Sensitive when the configuration holds a Sensitive value, such as the
encryption passphrase, so that it stays out of logs and reports.

Returns: `Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]` The YAML document.

##### `config`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Any]`

The borgmatic options.

## Data types

### <a name="Borgmatic--Action"></a>`Borgmatic::Action`

A borgmatic action, as named since borgmatic 1.9

Alias of `Enum['repo-create', 'transfer', 'prune', 'compact', 'create', 'recreate', 'check', 'delete', 'extract', 'config', 'export-tar', 'mount', 'umount', 'repo-delete', 'restore', 'repo-list', 'list', 'repo-info', 'info', 'break-lock', 'key', 'diff', 'browse', 'borg']`

### <a name="Borgmatic--Check"></a>`Borgmatic::Check`

A string is the name of the check, the other keys are those of the
`checks` option of borgmatic.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
'repository'
{ 'name' => 'repository', 'frequency' => '2 weeks', 'only_run_on' => ['Saturday'] }
```

Alias of

```puppet
Variant[Enum['repository', 'archives', 'data', 'extract', 'spot', 'disabled'], Struct[{
    'name'                                 => Enum['repository', 'archives', 'data', 'extract', 'spot', 'disabled'],
    Optional['frequency']                  => String[1],
    Optional['only_run_on']                => Array[String[1], 1],
    Optional['max_duration']               => Integer[1],
    Optional['count_tolerance_percentage'] => Numeric,
    Optional['data_sample_percentage']     => Numeric,
    Optional['data_tolerance_percentage']  => Numeric,
    Optional['xxh64sum_command']           => String[1],
  }]]
```

### <a name="Borgmatic--Command"></a>`Borgmatic::Command`

A command hook of a borgmatic configuration (borgmatic >= 2.0)

#### Examples

##### Dump a database before each backup

```puppet
{ 'before' => 'action', 'when' => ['create'], 'run' => ['/usr/local/bin/dump-db'] }
```

##### Report failures

```puppet
{ 'after' => 'error', 'run' => ['echo "{configuration_filename}: {error}" | mail root'] }
```

Alias of

```puppet
Variant[Struct[{
    'before'         => Enum['action', 'repository', 'configuration', 'everything'],
    Optional['when'] => Array[Borgmatic::Action, 1],
    'run'            => Array[String[1], 1],
  }], Struct[{
    'after'            => Enum['action', 'repository', 'configuration', 'everything', 'error'],
    Optional['when']   => Array[Borgmatic::Action, 1],
    Optional['states'] => Array[Enum['finish', 'fail'], 1],
    'run'              => Array[String[1], 1],
  }]]
```

### <a name="Borgmatic--Compression"></a>`Borgmatic::Compression`

A Borg compression specification

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
'zstd,3'
'auto,lzma,6'
```

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(none|lz4)\z/, /\A(zstd|zlib|lzma)(,\d{1,2})?\z/, /\Aauto,(lz4|zstd|zlib|lzma)(,\d{1,2})?\z/, /\Aobfuscate,\d+,.+\z/]`

### <a name="Borgmatic--Encryption"></a>`Borgmatic::Encryption`

The keyfile modes are left out: the key would stay on the server, where
the borgmatic client cannot use it.

Alias of `Enum['none', 'authenticated', 'authenticated-blake2', 'repokey', 'repokey-blake2']`

### <a name="Borgmatic--RepositoryEntry"></a>`Borgmatic::RepositoryEntry`

A string is the path of the repository, the other keys are those of the
`repositories` option of borgmatic.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
'ssh://borg@backup.example.org/srv/borg/client1'
{ 'path' => 'ssh://borg@backup.example.org/srv/borg/client1', 'label' => 'backup' }
```

Alias of

```puppet
Variant[String[1], Struct[{
    'path'                              => String[1],
    Optional['label']                   => String[1],
    Optional['encryption']              => String[1],
    Optional['append_only']             => Boolean,
    Optional['storage_quota']           => Borgmatic::StorageQuota,
    Optional['make_parent_directories'] => Boolean,
  }]]
```

### <a name="Borgmatic--Secret"></a>`Borgmatic::Secret`

A secret such as a passphrase or a password, optionally Sensitive

Alias of `Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]`

### <a name="Borgmatic--Settings"></a>`Borgmatic::Settings`

Used for the database, monitoring and snapshot hooks, whose many and
evolving keys are checked by borgmatic itself. Top-level values may be
Sensitive, for example a password.

Alias of `Hash[String[1], Variant[Data, Sensitive]]`

### <a name="Borgmatic--StorageQuota"></a>`Borgmatic::StorageQuota`

A Borg storage quota, a size with an optional unit suffix

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
'500G'
```

Alias of `Pattern[/\A\d+(\.\d+)?[KMGTPEZY]?\z/]`

### <a name="Borgmatic--Umask"></a>`Borgmatic::Umask`

It is a string so that its leading zero survives: Puppet reads an integer
literal such as `0027` as an octal number.

#### Examples

#####

```puppet
'0027'
```

Alias of `Pattern[/\A0?[0-7]{3}\z/]`

### <a name="Borgmatic--Verbosity"></a>`Borgmatic::Verbosity`

A borgmatic verbosity level, from -2 (disabled) to 2 (debug)

Alias of `Integer[-2, 2]`
